items.answerEvidence: Audio says a group of birds are flying away from the tree; only picture C shows the flock leaving the tree.
distractorAnalysis: A shows birds on the ground, while B shows birds gathered around a fountain rather than leaving a tree.

items.answerEvidence: The sentence says the boy and girl are shopping for bicycles; price tags and comparison in B show that action.
distractorAnalysis: A depicts repairing a bicycle, and C depicts riding bicycles, so neither matches shopping.

items.answerEvidence: The boy is crying because his ice cream dropped on the floor; picture C contains both the fallen ice cream and his reaction.
distractorAnalysis: A and B show the ice cream still on a table or in the boy's hand, so the stated accident has not happened.

items.answerEvidence: The speaker asks for the last name to be spelled because it was not understood; B directly provides the spelling.
distractorAnalysis: A gives a nickname and C comments on how common the name is; neither carries out the requested spelling.

items.answerEvidence: David is not home and the caller may leave a callback message; B naturally declines and says the cellphone will be tried instead.
distractorAnalysis: A asks for information the receiver need not provide, while C reverses who would call whom and does not fit the offer.

items.answerEvidence: The speaker thanks someone for finding the missing cat; My pleasure is the appropriate response, so A is correct.
distractorAnalysis: B discusses timing and C introduces another cat; neither responds to the gratitude being expressed.

items.answerEvidence: Someone politely says the occupied seat is theirs; Oh, sorry acknowledges the mistake and yields the seat, making A best.
distractorAnalysis: Don't worry would be spoken by the seat owner, and Take a seat does not address the speaker's claim.

items.answerEvidence: How much do you spend on food a day asks for a daily money amount; About 200 dollars in A supplies that information.
distractorAnalysis: B gives meal frequency, and C gives a restaurant offer rather than the person's daily spending.

items.answerEvidence: What do you want for your birthday asks for a desired thing or event; A big party in B answers it directly.
distractorAnalysis: Next week answers when, and It was great reports a past experience rather than a birthday wish.

items.answerEvidence: After presenting the museum, lunch, and market plan, What do you say asks for agreement; Sounds good to me in A fits.
distractorAnalysis: B denies speaking and C asks whether a plan exists even though one has just been given.

items.answerEvidence: May I take your order now is a server's question; Yes, I'd like a steak, please in B is the customer's suitable reply.
distractorAnalysis: A reverses the roles by giving permission to order, while C gives a bill total before any order is placed.

items.answerEvidence: Lucy reveals a new baby rabbit and is told she cannot keep a rabbit in the house; therefore the hidden animal is A.
distractorAnalysis: Fish are already known family pets, and a dog is mentioned only as a pet Lucy did not get.

items.answerEvidence: The woman calls the man the mouse and points to cream on his face, proving that the man ate the cake; B is correct.
distractorAnalysis: No real mouse moved the cake, and the woman had saved it for later rather than successfully protecting it.

items.answerEvidence: From the marked point, the route reaches Maple Street, turns right, walks one block, then turns left; the corner on the left is B.
distractorAnalysis: A is beyond the stated corner near King Street, while C lies on the wrong side and before the final left turn.

items.answerEvidence: The man reports losing a book he borrowed and staff ask for his name and the book title, which is a library procedure; A follows.
distractorAnalysis: A bookstore would discuss purchase or return, and a police station would not manage a borrowed-book record.

items.answerEvidence: Jenny says she will take a bus and tells Joe to go to the bakery and pick up the ordered cake, so C is the requested action.
distractorAnalysis: A is unnecessary because they will meet at Kevin's place, and B is explicitly cancelled when she says not to pick her up.

items.answerEvidence: She refuses because she does not want to step on and hurt his toes, implying that she believes she is a poor dancer; C is best.
distractorAnalysis: She does not need to leave and her own toes are not hurt; both A and B misread the reason given.

items.answerEvidence: They discuss who paid last time and who may pay next time; Let me get this therefore means the woman wants to buy the man's dinner, A.
distractorAnalysis: Dog care is why she wants to thank him, not the action she offers; the birthday gift is never the present bill.

items.answerEvidence: The speaker introduces Ms. Dale and Mr. Lee, praises their experience, and says they have joined the team; the good news is B.
distractorAnalysis: Better business is a future expectation, and no new department store is announced, ruling out A and C.

items.answerEvidence: Hair remained on the floor and dark marks remained on the wall after cleaning, so the man judges the cleaners bad at their job; A.
distractorAnalysis: The high price is mentioned by the other speaker, while the man's own evidence denies that the service was good.

items.answerEvidence: She says talking briefly to the waiter was more fun than lunch with Josh, which implies the lunch was boring; C is correct.
distractorAnalysis: A contradicts her negative comparison, and warm describes the water she requested rather than her feeling about lunch.
